title: Cross-plane compact KV partitioning with eviction hints for tensor/pipeline hybrids
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: As models scale across tensor- and pipeline-parallel boundaries, the KV cache footprint becomes fragmented and memory-inefficient. Existing slab/striping strategies either over-allocate per-GPU KV slabs or force expensive cross-GPU fetches during generation. This ticket proposes a compact, cross-plane KV partitioning scheme with lightweight eviction hints to reduce peak GPU memory and improve tail latency for mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies.
proposal: Introduce a compact cross-plane KV partition format that groups hot prefixes into contiguous micro-shards aligned with runtime pipeline stages, while storing per-shard eviction hints (approximate recency scores + prefix weight) in a small metadata plane. During generation, the scheduler consults eviction hints to prefer local micro-shards and trigger asynchronous prefetch for likely-needed remote shards. The scheme supports both: (a) tensor-parallel model shards (local KV per replica) and (b) pipeline stages (KV owned by stage nodes) with a single consistent addressing layer.
design_notes:
- Memory layout: micro-shards are sized ~8-64KB (configurable) to balance addressing overhead vs. compaction.
- Metadata plane: per-micro-shard 16B descriptor: last_access_ts (48-bit bucketed), prefix_weight (8-bit), flags (8-bit). Stored in device pinned memory and replicated across nodes for fast decisions.
- Addressing: global shard ID scheme (64-bit) mapping to (plane_id, gpu_index, offset).
- Migration: when a micro-shard becomes hot across multiple GPUs, policy allows lightweight replication of the micro-shard to at most 2 additional GPUs to avoid repeated transfers. Replication is GC'd based on hint decay.
- Eviction hints: approximate LRU implemented via exponentially decaying counters to minimize atomic updates.
- Interaction with continuous batching: batch router includes micro-shard hints to group requests that can reuse local micro-shards in the same batch.
- Fallback: if metadata unavailable, revert to current slab-striping behavior to ensure safety.
tradeoffs:
- Pros: lower peak KV memory, improved tail latency by avoiding large cross-GPU fetches, finer-grained replication for high fanout prefixes.
- Cons: additional metadata overhead, complexity in maintaining hint consistency, small extra CPU/host memory for metadata replication.
- Risk: wrong hint heuristics could cause more cross-GPU transfers; mitigated by conservative replication caps and telemetry-driven tuning.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime config; 2) Canary on non-critical model family (internal perf harness) with telemetry collection for 2 weeks; 3) Gradual ramp to dedicated clusters; 4) Enable for select customer workloads with opt-in.
Telemetry to collect: per-request remote-shard-fetch rate, average shard replication count, peak GPU KV memory, tail latency (p95/p99), failed prefetch rate.
acceptance_criteria:
- p95 generation latency for canonical 8k-context tests improves or stays within 5% of baseline.
- Peak KV memory usage reduced by >=12% on 16-GPU pipeline jobs for internal benchmark.
- Remote-shard-fetch rate reduced by >=20% for mixed fanout workloads.
- No correctness regressions (bit-identical outputs for deterministic eval) across test models.
- Unit/e2e tests and a canary dashboard created.
tasks: Spec micro-shard metadata format and API (runtime/host)
Implement compact micro-shard allocator and global ID mapping
Add eviction-hint counters and decaying update path
Integrate hint-aware batch router to prefer local micro-shards
Async prefetch worker for likely remote shards with backpressure
Replication policy and GC for micro-shards
Unit tests + deterministic generation e2e tests
updates: 2026-02-25: Initial design spike completed; micro-shard size sweep shows 16KB median offers best latency/memory tradeoff for 2 model families.
2026-03-02: Prototype allocator merged to branch feat/kv-microshard-allocator; basic metadata layout reviewed by Martin Cole (infra). Feedback: make metadata atomic updates lock-free.
2026-03-05: Scheduler integration prototype finished; early canary shows 10% reduction in remote fetches but CPU overhead increased ~6%. Exploring sampling updates for hints to reduce CPU.

2026-03-10: Decided to cap replication to 2 additional GPUs and use exponential decay with 1h half-life for hint scores. Customer-impact assessment flagged as high; coordinating canary with Solutions Eng.
2026-03-10: Added dependency on ENG-25681 for async prefetch backpressure primitives.
review_feedback: Martin Cole: Prefer lock-free hint updates; suggested using per-thread buffers with periodic reduction.
Leah Ortiz (ML Infra): Ensure deterministic fallback path for eval runs to maintain reproducible outputs.
Samir Gupta (SRE): Add circuit-breaker to disable replication when network link errors spike.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for metadata encode/decode, allocation and GC.
- Integration tests with small multi-gpu simulation (4 GPUs) to validate addressing and prefetch.
- Perf regression tests run on perf harness with 8k/32k tokens.
- Canary run for 2 weeks with telemetry; automated rollback if remote-fetch spike >10% or p99 latency regresses >10%.
notes: This ticket targets a midsize engineering effort expected to touch runtime allocator, scheduler, and telemetry. Coordinate with product for customer opt-in and with solutions for canary selection. Keep feature behind clear runtime flags and runtime-1.21 release train.
